reader.requirement: At --std 85, with INVALID KEY specified, an invalid key condition on an indexed file must not run the associated USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure. Control goes to the INVALID KEY imperative; an explicit transfer (GO TO) inside it is obeyed; otherwise control passes to the end of the statement and NOT INVALID KEY is ignored. Nested delimited-scope statements and PERFORM inside the imperative must run by their own rules. The witness (a relative file, accepted at 85 and 2023) covers phrase-with-USE and the not-invalid arms; it does not cover indexed files, GO TO out of the imperative, nested I-O statements, or PERFORM.

reader.notes: EmitPhrasePair renders if (2x) { imperative } else if (0x && gate) { NOT imperative }, so NOT INVALID KEY never follows an invalid key. The __IoCheck body passes invalidKeyHandled and returns before the declarative tiers for the 2x family. Every arm of the rule was observed on an indexed file at 85.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IX.1.3.5 GR2 and the 1985 USE format (line 21048: USE [GLOBAL] AFTER STANDARD ... ON {file-name|INPUT|OUTPUT|I-O|EXTEND}). r3.cob (r3-001): with INVALID KEY specified, neither the open-mode USE ON OUTPUT nor the USE GLOBAL ON I-O ran (IK-OUT 22 then AFTER-OUT with no USE line; IK-IO 22 then AFTER-IO; IN-IK 22 then IN-AFTER in the nested program; IK-DEL, IK-RDA and IN-IK-RW with no USE line), NOT INVALID KEY was ignored (no NIK-OUT or IN-NIK), and control reached the end of the statement; the same statements without the phrase ran the matching USE (USE-OUT, USE-IO, and USE-IO from the nested program), so the phrase and not the declarative selection decides. 1985-only forms exercised: USE GLOBAL and the open-mode USE with STANDARD omitted (optional in 1985's format). cite.py: 'OK §1985:IX.1.3.5 GR2 (1.3.5 The Invalid Key Condition) the text is in GR2'.
